lines.say: 100+ databases in 25 MB, with no Java JRE to install first.
DBX is a lightweight, cross-platform database client built in Rust, with a desktop app, Docker, a CLI and built-in AI.
It connects to MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, MongoDB, DuckDB, ClickHouse and SQL Server from one tool.
You describe what you want in plain language, and the AI SQL assistant gives you SQL back.
The query editor runs on CodeMirror 6, with metadata-aware autocomplete and 9 editor themes.
A virtual-scrolled data grid handles large result sets, and you can import CSV or Excel files.
A separate Rust-powered MCP server lets coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor query your databases through DBX.
Destructive operations need a confirmation, and connection credentials are encrypted.
The repo has 25.4k stars, and DBX is free and open source under Apache-2.0.
On a Mac, run brew install --cask dbx, or start the web version with Docker on port 4224.
